steps.description: NORTHPOLE\Administrator authenticated to DC01 via Kerberos ticket
Domain admin logon to DC01 confirmed

payload.text: A macro-enabled Office document opened by a user on WS01 spawned PowerShell, which immediately accessed the LSASS process to dump credential material. The attacker reused the extracted Kerberos ticket to authenticate to DC01 as a domain administrator, completing a pass-the-ticket lateral movement to the Domain Controller.
key_findings: PowerShell launched by WINWORD read LSASS memory on WS01 (LSASS Memory, T1003.001), indicating in-memory credential theft.
A Kerberos ticket from WS01 authenticated to DC01 as NORTHPOLE\Administrator (Pass the Ticket, T1550.003).
The chain terminates at the Domain Controller, so the blast radius is the entire domain.
hypotheses: Credential material may have been exfiltrated before network telemetry began capturing outbound traffic.
Additional workstations may have been compromised using the same ticket before DC01 authentication was observed.

actions.rationale: WS01 is the entry point and the source of the stolen ticket; isolating it halts further reuse.

actions.action: Revoke active Kerberos tickets issued to WS01 and reset the krbtgt account twice.
actions.rationale: A stolen TGT stays valid until tickets are invalidated, even after the host is contained.

actions.action: Force-reset NORTHPOLE\Administrator and every account with recent Kerberos activity from WS01.
actions.rationale: These credentials are presumed compromised after the LSASS dump.

actions.action: Hunt for lateral movement originating from DC01 after timestamp 1749100090.
actions.rationale: DC01 access may have been used to pivot further into the domain.
